correctness.rationale: The complete finite-population jump generator was independently enumerated on 48 rational state/parameter configurations. Its closed second-moment system is proved by exact ordered-pair summation; eigenvalues are strictly negative since the trace is negative, the determinant is \(\mu^3/[2(N-1)]>0\), and the discriminant is positive. The exact disagreement formula matches \(D_N(0)=0\) and \(D_N^{\prime}(0)>0\), yielding a unique maximum. Fixed-parameter eigenvalue expansions give the logarithmic and population-scale statements. Bounded martingale convergence and U(infinity)=1 prove finite-N unanimity; the Lipschitz x^2/2 observable gives the explicit positive W1 obstruction. No finite search is used as proof of an infinite statement. Numerical asymptotic checks are supporting evidence only.

value.rationale: The original model has an analytically striking nontrivial Bernoulli-convolution mean-field equilibrium and an explicit desire for uniform-in-time finite-population approximation. An exact two-timescale finite-N observable resolves how apparent opinion fragmentation coexists with eventual consensus. The logarithmic peak and mu-dependent exponential N-scale envelope quantify the length of the physically observable quasi-stationary regime; the strict W1 lower bound disproves a natural uniform-marginal approximation. This is not a routine constant extraction from the known mean-field variance, and it provides practical calibration for simulation horizons.
